title: An ended version and a whole experience

captions.physics: Matching an outcome to different observations
captions.emotions: Feeling wholeness in a discovered meaning

meaning: Accurate examination can make your shared view more coherent by ending an explanation that failed to include different aspects of actual experience.
text: Wholeness can appear after a familiar assessment of completeness ends. Justice in the physical position of Ajna suggests matching an outcome to different observations. Death in energy supports ending an overly narrow explanation. The World in emotions responds with wholeness in a discovered meaning. You enjoy seeing experience preserve its significant aspects.

For example, part of an exhibition is inaccessible and the visit initially seems incomplete. Comparing impressions reveals a connected account within the open rooms. **A whole meaning can survive after a narrow criterion of completion ends.** A complete programme becomes distinguishable from experience’s content. The part you could not visit remains a real limitation within your understanding of the experience. Pleasure comes through an assembled picture without pretending you saw everything. Both sides make your view more honest: you can name what was missing and what you actually understood together.

The risk is declaring every limitation necessarily useful after that discovery. Another explanation exceeds the facts. Willingness to end exhausted versions can preserve proportion again. Some experience happened while another part remains unknown. Wholeness need not give it a hidden positive meaning. Your view can hold that distinction, preserve discovered connections and leave another case its own question beyond an answer decided beforehand.
